limitations: Reviewer is a separate AI agent session on the same host and the same operator account as the producer. It is not a second machine, a second operator, or a human. It ran no harness, used no network, changed no git state and no repository file, and read nothing outside the repository and the frozen code snapshot (commit d30db63). The work was done in three rounds; the v4 round is a delta review on top of the full v3 review by the same reviewer id.

Two earlier sets were rejected by this reviewer. Set v1 (2026-10-04, 67.7): the capture listed only brain/, so the root was not proved complete and ten rows (two root rows, eight native_absent rows) were unproven; the conversation database was not captured. Set v3 (2026-10-05, 82.9): duplicate safety counted three events as stated once that the last gen_metadata row states again (two thinking-only model steps, and the turn-2 system notice counted from the copy only), which made the score about 0.21 points too high; the adapter document named build 1.2.16 for runs of build 1.2.17 and did not disclose the self-update; one link-target hash confirmed an aliased log file name. Set v2 was not reviewed. Set v4 fixes the three v3 defects. A defect that this reviewer cannot see may still exist.

The captures were made by the producer on 2026-10-05, after the rule changes of 2026-10-03 to 2026-10-05, with a controller that was changed after the v1 rejection. Runs 02, 03, 04 are the first three captures that the whole-state controller completed. Attempt 01 of that day ran one turn and then stopped closed on an unexplained touch of the empty crashes/ directory; it is disclosed and not scored. The CLI updated itself from 1.2.16 to 1.2.17 during attempt 01, so the stopped attempt and the scored runs are different builds; in run 1 the updater still rewrote one binary. All 2026-10-04 attempts are superseded. Capture completeness and acquisition authenticity are the producer's retained receipts, not facts witnessed by the reviewer. The reviewer re-ran verify_state_capture on the raw receipts of both turns of each run (v3 round) and re-derived the classification from the public inventories (v4 round).

Model. The requested model is claude-sonnet-4-6 (--model, no effort flag, no --sandbox flag by owner decision). The stream init event and every gen_metadata row name that model. This is the vendor's own statement; no independent channel confirms which model served the calls.

Root. The runs used the operator's normal profile. The whole CLI state directory was listed by metadata; only files whose path carries the new conversation id were copied and hash-bound. Shared stores that changed and hold the operator's other conversations (conversation_summaries.db, jetbox_summaries_proto.pb, cache/last_conversations.json, cache/onboarding.json, bin/agentapi, the cli.log link, the touched crashes/ directory) were recorded by metadata only. portable.complete_root is therefore a contradiction (0 of 3 points), as in the Codex CLI row, and portable.companions is measured for the id-named family. The release code path is the same as for Codex CLI: the blocker portable_archive:hard_gate is recorded for each repetition and does not block the rank.

Absence path. attribution.token_semantics (0 of 2, two records decoded) and attribution.reconciliation are native_absent without a complete root, under the rubric sentence added on 2026-10-05 (complete id-named family plus the bound rows of every shared store that names the session). By owner decision the rows of the three test conversations were read from conversation_summaries.db and jetbox_summaries_proto.pb after the captures; they are in the packets, bound by content and not by a capture-time hash. Reviewer checks: every protobuf field of the extract is in the documented map (29 leaves, no token, cost or model field); the growth of jetbox_summaries_proto.pb in the public inventories equals the framed length of the extract entry (1010, 1017, 999 bytes); the summary's last-modified time is 29 to 40 ms before the capture-time mtime of the store; the usage message of all 25 model calls has no field 4 in any of its four copies and no row holds a turn or session total; the private process logs hold no count; the private implicit file was written before the first model call and not changed later.

Open point of the absence path. A third shared store names each session: cache/last_conversations.json. Its entry is NOT in the packets, and the adapter document inside the packets still says it was not read. Two things support the absence: (a) from public bytes alone, the file grew by exactly 167 bytes in each run, which is the workspace path (121) plus the conversation id (36) plus 10 bytes of JSON punctuation, so the entry has no room for a count; (b) after the packets were built the coordinator exported, by owner permission, a description of the one entry per run (private file last-conversations-entry.json beside each capture): the key is the workspace path and the value is the conversation id string, nothing else. The reviewer read these three files. They describe the entry and do not hold its key. The reviewer accepts this as a stated limitation, not a defect, because the public metadata already bounds the entry. The entry should be bound into the packets and the document sentence corrected at the next rebuild. A reader who requires the literal rubric wording inside the packet would hold these two rows unresolved; the row would then be provisional (82.7 to 89.7).

Protobuf. The vendor publishes no schema. Fields are named by number, by matching values with the stdout stream (usage fields 2, 3 and 5 equal the stream's input, output and cache-read counts for every model call) and by content. Field 4 of the usage message is read as the place of a cache-write count only by its absence and by analogy; a missing key earns no credit under the rubric in any case. gen_metadata 1.9.10 and 1.2.4 are context-size estimates and equal no sum of usage counts. Timestamps are protobuf seconds and nanoseconds; unit and zone are declared by the adapter document only.

Judgments that carry points. Version rows (4 points): PRAGMA user_version is 1 and the decoder refuses another value; only one value was ever observed. Self-contained identity (2 points): the harness comes from prompt prose in the last gen_metadata row and the surface from a directory name inside a stored path; the sanitizer keeps the identity prompt section for this. broad.standard_tools_readable is 0 because every record body is protobuf without a published schema. Duplicate safety is 0 of 16, 20, 20 events (37, 47, 47 occurrences; reviewer recount on raw rows agrees): gen_metadata is in the read because the decoder takes model identity from it; with the steps table alone the metric would be about 1.4 points higher but model identity (3 points) could not be claimed. Density is 0.219, 0.232, 0.237; sqlite_master rows are not in the denominator (effect below 0.01 points).

Public database. It is a sanitized derivative of equal size. On a scratch copy a stock SQLite reader gives integrity_check ok, the same schema and the same rows as the private database; every changed byte is inside a stated string or bytes field (home and account aliases; request configuration; system prompt, tool definitions and prompt sections except identity; the installation-level session number; the 404-byte client blob; executor_metadata strings) and the protobuf layout is unchanged. The reviewer's own page walk finds zero non-zero bytes outside headers, cell pointers, live cells, live overflow payload and the 4-byte headers of free blocks; there is no free-list page and no tail. A public reader cannot check the private digests of the family: the receipt digests of the database and inventories are those of the public bytes.

Public safety. The reviewer found no home user name, repository account name, account e-mail or its local part, host name or person name in 215 public files (plain, any case, UTF-16, hex, base64, URL-encoded, reversed; also across stream text deltas and inside the hex-encoded extract), no e-mail or token pattern, and no id of another conversation. Of 330 distinct 64-hex values, 252 are digests of public bytes, 72 are digests of public line digests, 3 are replay output digests, 2 are fixture digests and 1 is zero; none equals a digest of private-only content with the real names put back (files, lines, JSON sub-documents, strings, database pages, rows and BLOBs, depth 1 to 3), and none equals the hash of a guessable log file name (every second of three days, four path forms). Every link-target hash is zero. The reviewer did not know account ids or tokens and could search only for patterns.

Content that stays public: conversation, trajectory, workspace, project, execution and system-message ids; the names of the run's implicit files and log files with start times; provider request and response ids, tool call ids and thinking signatures, which the vendor can map to the account; the repository name and branch name; generated titles; the vendor tool list and notice texts; directory listings of the workspace in run 3; the length of the home name; the local time offset; the Python install path; for about 45 other conversations and other files of the profile: device and inode numbers, first-level directory, name lengths, tree shape and counts. Whether to publish these is an owner decision.

The packet manifests, replay receipts and the producer summary still say public_safe: false and independent_reproduction: false. This review is an attestation by an agent; it does not change those fields and is not an independent reproduction on a second environment. 74 Antigravity tests pass on the snapshot; 12 need artifact files that the snapshot does not hold.
